AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE MAHARLIKA INVESTMENT FUND,
PROVIDING FOR THE MANAGEMENT, INVESTMENT, AND USE
OF THE PROCEEDS OF THE FUND, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Maharlika Investment Fund Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to create a Maharlika Investment Fund (MIF) which shall be sourced from the investible funds of the country´s top performing Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), from contributions of the National Government, from the declared dividends of the BSP and other sources of funds to promote economic growth and social development.
Establishes an independent corporate body known as the Maharlika Investment Corporation (MIC) that shall act as vehicle for the mobilization and utilization of the MIF for investments in transactions that will enable to reap optimal returns on investments (ROIs) and govern and manage the Fund in accordance with the objectives and purposes of this Act.
Provides for the initial capitalization to be sourced as follows: 1.) Land Bank of the Philippines - Fifty billion pesos (P50 billion); and 2.) Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP) - Twenty-five billion pesos (P25 billion). 
Enumerates allowable and prohibited investments by the Maharlika Investment Corporation.
Mandates the creation of a Risk Management Unit (RMU) within the MIC to ensure that measures are taken to achieve a prudent balance between risk and reward in business activities, and that a risk-informed approach is observed with respect to the capitalization of the MIC.

AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE GUIDELINES FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT AND
OPERATION OF LOCAL UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES
rows.title_short: Local Universities And Colleges ( L U Cs ) Governance Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to prescribe mandatory guidelines on the establishment of local collages and the conversion of local collages into universities to achieve a standard and integrated system of higher education, provide the appropriate direction in their governance, and ensure that they will deliver quality and relevant education to students.
Provides for the establishment of a local Higher education institution (HEI) to be known as a local college or dalubhasaan to be operated by the LGU through an ordinance duly enacted by the sanggunian with consultation with the Commission on Higher Education.
Grants the CHED to exercise supervisory power to monitor, inspect, evaluate, and provide assistance to local universities and colleges and to devise ways and practices that will ensure that the LUCs will remain committed to the delivery of quality education to its students.
Provides for the leadership structure of the Local Higher Education Institutions and Local Universities and Colleges and their duties and powers of the Board.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT TO PROTECT MARINE MAMMALS AND ENSURE THEIR SURVIVAL FOR THE
BENEFIT OF FUTURE GENERATIONS
rows.abstract:
Seeks, among others, the following: 
To hasten the government´s response in undertaking management measures for critically endangered marine mammals such as Irrawaddy dolphins of Negros Occidental;  to undertake research on the current status of other marine mammals in the country to be able to develop conservation plans as well as sustainable ecotourism projects; to clarify the law concerning the import/export of marine mammals; to fully explore the economic potential and benefit of dolphin/whale watching industry; to strengthen the role of scientists, conservationists as advisory bodies to government agencies, etc.

Proposes to create the Marine Mammal Protection and Conservation Committee (MMPCC) with the following functions, among others, related to: 
research programs for conservation purposes; manuals and protocols for the rescue of stranded animals; manuals and guidelines for sustainable dolphin and whale-watching tours; technical assessments of rescued, stranded or rehabilitated marine mammals; conservation and management measures of critically endangered or vulnerable marine mammals; Marine Protected Areas and Networks and Marine Corridors; Important Marine Mammal Areas (IMMAs) as designated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and the Marine Mammal Protected Areas Task Force (MMPATF)

rows.title_short: Granting Full Insurance Coverage To All Qualified Agrarian Reform Beneficiaries Of The Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 6657, As Amended By Republic Act No. 9700, Otherwise Known As The “ Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law Of 1988”
rows.abstract:
Seeks to grant full insurance coverage for compensable losses to all qualified agrarian reform beneficiaries who are defined in Section 3(b) of the “Agri-Agra Reform Credit Act of 2009.”
Covers the loses resulting from the natural calamities; plant diseases; pest infestations and loss of life or inquiry due to accident.
Covers the following crops and other farming and fishery produce such as: 1. Palay, corn, sugarcane, high-value crops as defined in Section 4(b) of RA 7900 or the “High-Value Crops Development Act of 1995´, coconut, tobacco; 2. Crops or stocks in fisheries farms; 3. Livestock; and 4. Non-crop agricultural assets used In actual farming and reported to and certified by the DAR.
Mandates the Secretary of the DA and the Secretary of the DAR to immediately include in their Departments´ Programs the operationalization of the insurance coverage.

rows.title_short: National Citizens Service Training Program Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to train and mobilize for the youth´s holistic development; institutionalize their vital role in nation-building; encourage their early involvement in public and civic affairs; and develop a citizenry that is ready to defend the State in personal and military service. 
Establishes the National Citizens Service Training Program (NCST) which shall be implemented by the CHED in all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and by the TESDA in all Technical-Vocational Institutions (TVIs) in consultation with the Department of National Defense.
Mandates the administration of NSTP to all students enrolled in undergraduate degree program in all public and privates HEIs and at least two-year programs in all TVIs in the Philippines. 
Mandates NCST to be a requisite for graduation of covered tertiary education students, however, the CHED or TESDA, based on the rules recommended by the NCST Technical Panel, shall, prescribe alternative NCST Programs to address students with special needs and persons with disabilities.
Establishes a Reserve Officers´ Training Corps (ROTC) Program, an optional four (4) year military training program designed to provide military training to students enrolled in undergraduate degree programs in HEIs who have expressed interest or shown potential to be officers of the AFP Regular and Reserve Force (Citizen Armed Force).Provides maximum penalty for any abuse, corruption, hazing, torture, data privacy rights violation, or violation of human rights committed in direct or indirect relation to the implementation of this Act.
